bib.title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models

question: To what extent can LLM planners reason over closed-loop environment feedback given in natural language, without extra training, to improve robot instruction completion?
hypothesis: Injecting success, object and scene feedback as text into the LLM prompt (an 'inner monologue') improves robustness and long-horizon planning over open-loop LLM planning.
contributions: Inner Monologue: a general formulation that chains perception models, pretrained skills and human feedback in a shared language prompt
Study of feedback sources (success detection, passive and active scene description, human) in three domains: sim tabletop, real tabletop, real kitchen mobile manipulation
Qualitative emergent capabilities: adapting to new instructions, self-proposed goals, multilingual input, scene Q&A

method.summary: A frozen LLM plans skills step by step with few-shot prompts; after each step textual feedback (success, visible objects, achieved sub-goals, human answers) is appended to the prompt so the LLM can retry or replan. Three instantiations use different LLMs, skills and feedback modules.
method.task: LLM-based high-level planning for language-conditioned robot manipulation

datasets.name: Sim tabletop rearrangement (Ravens-based)
datasets.source: Ravens simulator; up to 4 blocks and up to 3 bowls, 10 colours, 9 locations, 15cm minimum spacing
datasets.preprocessing: Gaussian noise at test time: N(0,3) pixel observation, N(0,2.5) policy heatmaps, N(0,0.02m) place locations

datasets.name: Low-level policy demonstrations (sim)
datasets.source: expert pick/place from ground-truth simulator poses

datasets.name: Real tabletop rearrangement
datasets.source: UR5e arm, wrist RealSense RGB-D; three 4cm cubes; 3 fruits, 3 bottles, 3 plates
datasets.preprocessing: Policy noise: planar pick translation, magnitude Normal sigma=1.5cm (stacking) or 0.7cm (sorting), capped at 1.5 sigma (Appendix A.2); main text says sigma=4mm clipped at 2 sigma

datasets.name: Kitchen mobile manipulation (SayCan setup)
datasets.source: Everyday Robots mobile manipulator, office kitchen, 15 household items, 5 locations

models.name: InstructGPT (sim and real tabletop planner)
models.architecture: GPT-3 fine-tuned with human feedback, via OpenAI API

models.name: Foresight/hindsight success detector (kitchen)
models.architecture: CLIP image/text encoders + fusion MLPs, fine-tuned; BCE for foresight, CLIP symmetric contrastive loss for hindsight

inference.samples: Sim: 50 episodes per task; real tabletop: 10 runs per task; kitchen: 120 evaluations total; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Few-shot prompts with no fine-tuning; format varies per domain (Robot thought / Robot action / Scene; robot.pick_place with Successful action; numbered steps with [success: no][scene: ...]); max steps k=15 in sim

parameters.sim_success_rule: 2D distance <4cm and picked object higher than place object

metrics.name: Task success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of episodes/runs completing the instruction (binary reward from ground truth in sim)

baselines: LLM with Object feedback only (open loop)
eval.protocol: Averaged over 50 episodes (sim), 10 runs (real tabletop), 120 evaluations (kitchen); no significance tests; kitchen adds adversarial human disturbances forcing skill failure

availability.code: Project website https://innermonologue.github.io (no code release stated)

prompts.text:
Scene: There is a cyan, yellow, brown block.
Human: Move all the blocks to the top left corner.
Robot thought: Goal state is ["Cyan block is
on the top left corner.", ...]
Robot action: Pick the cyan block and place it on the top left corner.
Scene: You have completed ["Cyan block is on the top left corner."]
prompts.where: Appendix D, Listing 1 (full prompts in paper)

prompts.text:
Robot: Hi there, I’m a robot operating in an office kitchen.
You can ask me to do various tasks and I’ll tell you the sequence of actions I would do to accomplish your task.
Human: hold the snickers
Robot: 1. pick up the snickers[success: no][scene: snickers]
prompts.where: Appendix D, Listing 3 (Listings 2 and 4 also in paper)

limits: Oracle scene descriptors (humans or scripted) assumed in Sec 4.1 and 4.3; learned versions only checked in Table 5
Failure sources: success detector errors (false negatives cause retries, false positives add partial observability), LLM planning errors, control errors
LLM planners sometimes ignored feedback and proposed skills with absent objects
Low-level policies bottleneck what the LLM can achieve
Emergent capabilities are inconsistent without similar prompt examples
Small trial counts (10 runs real tabletop), no confidence intervals or seeds
Different LLMs, skills and feedback per domain, so cross-domain comparisons are not controlled
Sim and kitchen results use InstructGPT 1.3B and PaLM-540B, both dated

terms.definition: binary classification of whether the low-level skill has succeeded, given to the LLM in language form
sources of scene feedback consistently provided and structured, injected without querying by the LLM planner
feedback provided in response to active queries by the LLM planner, unstructured answers
